claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified for launch now, on a narrow launch-readiness basis, despite a 2.1-point miss on the Spanish-language billing support segment.
decision_criteria: Use policy-specific predicates over general governance guidance when they conflict in specificity.
Treat named customer commitments and named launch use cases as material unless admissible evidence resolves that status.
Do not accept product non-core or low-volume framing as sufficient to defeat materiality when policy says otherwise.
Certification is compliant only if the material limitation was resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
evidence_requests: Approved risk acceptance covering the Spanish-language billing support gap before launch.
Final legal determination on whether the gap must be disclosed.
Executed model-card or launch disclosure showing the limitation was disclosed for the named launch use case.
Evidence that the three international pilot commitments are not contractual customer commitments or not named launch use cases under policy.
Evidence the 2.1-point gap was remediated and re-tested to target before certification.
specific_concerns: Admissible evidence shows the affected Spanish-language billing support segment is named in three international pilot commitments, which points to materiality under the stated policy.
The policy text says product labels such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when the affected segment is named in customer commitments or when legal review is pending.
The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
There is admissible evidence of an open legal review on whether disclosure is required, with no final answer.
No admissible evidence shows the gap was resolved before launch.
No admissible evidence shows an approved risk acceptance before launch.
No admissible evidence shows the required disclosure was completed.
unsupported_claims: That current certification is policy-compliant based on aggregate readiness and clean rehearsal evidence alone.
That the 5% projected traffic characterization is sufficient to treat the weakness as non-material.
That public governance principles about measurement and monitoring are enough to satisfy the repo-specific disclosure predicate for a named launch use case.
